uncertain_sources: The board briefly omits the minus sign in the one-spin average energy. The chapter retains the live correction and uses the thermodynamic sign consistently.
The lecture calls the nearest-neighbor correlation the better-than-even probability. The chapter distinguishes correlation two-p-minus-one from the same-spin probability p.
The board alternates between n and n-minus-one for endpoint separation. The chapter defines r as the number of intervening bonds and uses tanh(beta J) to the r.
The antiferromagnetic sign map is exact for an open chain and an even periodic chain. The chapter states the boundary qualification omitted in the spoken shorthand.
The mean-field graph momentarily suppresses the negative magnetized branch even though positive J does not choose a global orientation. The chapter restores both symmetry-related branches.
The spoken direction of the temperature inequality near the transition reverses once. The chapter uses the consistent high-temperature disordered and low-temperature ordered assignment.
Broken bonds are counted as abstract units on the board. The chapter restores their energy cost of two J, giving eight J for one square-lattice flip and four J for a one-dimensional block.
The external-field sign changes during the board derivation. The chapter chooses H equals minus J pair sum minus h spin sum, with positive h favoring positive spins.
The finite-system zero-average mixture and spontaneous magnetization are conflated in the live discussion. The chapter states the thermodynamic-limit order explicitly.

The Earth-reversal discussion is openly uncertain and informally describes core current reversal. The chapter preserves the question while bounding the analogy with the modern liquid-outer-core geodynamo account.
